title: Turkic expansion across Eurasia
summary: A study of ancient DNA finds that historical events, including short-lived khanates in the Medieval period, transformed the Eurasian steppes from being home to Indo-European speakers to the mostly Turkic-speaking groups of the present day. Turkic peoples were among those who settled the Orkhon Valley in Mongolia, which holds archaeological remains dating back to the 6th century.

uncertainty.note: Bumin Qaghan established the First Turkic Khaganate in 552 CE; UNESCO notes Turkish memorial sites of the 6th-7th centuries in the Orkhon Valley before the 8th-century rise of the Uighurs.

as_recorded.value: Turkish memorial sites of the 6th-7th centuries

where.modern_name: Eurasian steppe; pin at Orkhon Valley, Mongolia
where.historical_name: Ötüken / Orkhon River basin, imperial heartland of the Türk Qaghanate

importance.justification: Turkic-speaking peoples came to dominate much of the Eurasian steppe.

sources.title: 137 ancient human genomes from across the Eurasian steppes
sources.author: Peter de Barros Damgaard et al.

reviewer_note: Dates are approximate and mark early Turkic presence in the Orkhon Valley, not a single start. The genetic evidence dates the change only broadly. The pin marks the Orkhon Valley.
